Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

role noun

a function, the part someone plays

also function, play a part, it’s your job to, part to play

classical

Cic. Fam. 11.5.3: tuum est hoc mūnus, tuae partēs
Cic. de Or. 2.26: Antōniī audiō esse partēs, ut dē tōtā ēloquentiā disserat (Lewis & Short)

partēs, partium f. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

one’s part, role, function

Plural. “It’s your job to …” is tuum est, or tuae partēs sunt with ut.

Other words

  • mūnus, mūneris n. — task, function, duty

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.20: jūstitiae prīmum mūnus est ut nē cui quis noceat

    The task that falls to someone or something.

  • persōna, persōnae f. — the part one plays in life

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.194: neque āctor sim aliēnae persōnae, sed auctor meae (Lewis & Short)

    The character or part a person sustains.

  • potentia, potentiae f. — function (of a word, in grammar)

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · Traupman 319

Examples

  • tuum est hoc mūnus, tuae partēs, ā tē hoc cīvitās vel omnēs potius gentēs nōn exspectant sōlum sed etiam postulant

    this is your task, your role: the state, or rather all nations, not only expect it of you but demand itCic. Fam. 11.5.3

  • jūstitiae prīmum mūnus est ut nē cui quis noceat nisi lacessītus injūriā

    the first role of justice is that no one should harm another unless provoked by a wrongCic. Off. 1.20

See also role, mission, position, represent.
